stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In 1932, the conductor Vera Holt made a single change to the way her orchestra performed Brahms's symphonies, and critics soon remarked on a leaner, quicker sound. ______ she required the string players to use gut strings instead of steel ones, reviving a practice that had been common in Brahms's own lifetime.
explanation: The first sentence mentions one vague thing, 'a single change.' The sentence after the blank says exactly what that change was: switching to gut strings. Nothing is picked out of a larger group. The second sentence just states the same change more precisely, so 'Specifically' is the right transition.

A.why: You treated the gut-string rule as one change out of several. The passage says Holt made 'a single change,' so there is no group to take an example from. The second sentence spells out that one change.

B.why: You read a contrast that isn't there. The gut-string rule doesn't go against anything in the first sentence. It explains the change the first sentence mentions.

C.why: You read the sentences as steps in time. The gut-string rule is the change itself, not something Holt did after making it.

subtype_name: General claim, then the detail (For example vs Specifically / In particular)

rated_why: Specification of the single change mentioned.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Folklorist Ines Varga found that the flood legends told in villages along the Tisza River share several recurring motifs, even when the villages are more than a hundred miles apart. ______ in at least eleven of the versions she recorded, a stranger warns the townspeople the night before the water rises, and only one family heeds the warning.
explanation: The first sentence names a group: 'several recurring motifs.' The sentence after the blank describes one of them, the stranger's warning that only one family heeds. Giving one member of a larger group is the job of 'For example.'

A.why: You treated the second sentence as a rewording of the first. It adds something new and narrower: one particular motif out of several. It doesn't say the first claim again in different words.

C.why: You chose a contrast word, but the stranger motif supports the claim that the legends share motifs. It doesn't push against it.

D.why: You read a cause and effect. Sharing motifs doesn't cause the stranger motif to appear. The stranger motif is one of the shared motifs.

subtype_name: General claim, then the detail (For example vs Specifically / In particular)

rated_why: Example of the recurring motifs mentioned.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Engineers at a laboratory in Zurich have improved upon a common method for making glass resistant to cracking. ______ rather than cooling the hot glass rapidly with jets of air, they immerse it in a bath of molten potassium salt, which forces larger ions into the surface and leaves it tightly compressed.
explanation: The first sentence makes a general claim about one thing: the engineers 'improved upon a common method.' The sentence after the blank explains exactly what that improvement was, the salt bath in place of air cooling. It describes the same improvement in more detail, so 'Specifically' fits.

B.why: You took the salt bath to be one of several improvements. The passage describes one improved method, and the second sentence explains what that method is.

C.why: You chose a contrast word, but the salt-bath process doesn't go against the claim of improvement. It is the improvement.

D.why: You read the second sentence as a result of the first. The salt bath isn't a consequence of the improvement. It is what the improvement consists of.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Historian Rana Qadir argues that indigo dyers in eighteenth-century Bengal developed many techniques for controlling the depth of color in finished cloth. ______ some dyers dipped a length of cotton as many as twenty times, letting it oxidize in the open air between baths so that each immersion darkened the blue slightly.
explanation: The first sentence names a group, 'many techniques.' The sentence after the blank describes one of them: repeated dipping with oxidation between baths. Since the second sentence gives one member of a larger group, 'For example' is correct.

A.why: You treated the dipping method as a rewording of 'many techniques.' It is one new, specific technique. It doesn't explain what the whole claim means.

B.why: You chose a word that signals something happening at the same time or a side topic. The dipping method belongs to the same subject and is part of the claim.

D.why: You read a contrast, but the dipping technique supports Qadir's claim about color-control techniques. It doesn't oppose it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Researchers studying why some people shake off a common cold virus faster than others have traced the difference to one feature of the early immune response. ______ fast recoverers produce interferon in the lining of the nose within hours of infection, while slow recoverers take more than a day to do so.
explanation: The first sentence mentions 'one feature' but doesn't say what it is. The sentence after the blank names it: how quickly interferon is produced in the nose. The sentence spells out that single feature exactly rather than picking one item from a set, so 'Specifically' is correct.

A.why: You treated the interferon timing as one example among several. The passage says the difference comes from 'one feature,' and the second sentence tells you what that feature is.

C.why: You chose a word that sets up an alternative or a condition. The second sentence doesn't describe what would happen otherwise. It identifies the feature just mentioned.

D.why: You chose a word that brings in a parallel second point. The interferon detail isn't a separate, similar finding. It is the same finding, stated more precisely.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In 2019 the town of Marlow adopted a single rule that its health officials credit with halving hospital visits for heatstroke. ______ public swimming pools and libraries must remain open until 10 p.m. on any day the temperature exceeds 95°F, giving residents without air conditioning a cool place to wait out the evening.
explanation: The first sentence refers to 'a single rule' without saying what it requires. The sentence after the blank states the rule in full. It is the same rule described precisely, not one picked from several, so 'Specifically' is correct.

B.why: You treated the late-hours requirement as one rule out of several. The passage says Marlow adopted 'a single rule,' and the second sentence explains what it is.

C.why: You read the second sentence as replacing something. Nothing is being swapped out. The late-hours requirement is the rule the first sentence mentions.

D.why: You read a time order. The requirement describes the 2019 rule itself, not something that happened before it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Planners in Medellín, Colombia, have tried several ways of connecting the city's steep hillside neighborhoods to jobs and services downtown. ______ in 2004 the city opened a cable-car line that carries commuters above slopes too sharp for ordinary buses to climb easily.
explanation: The first sentence names a group, 'several ways' of connecting neighborhoods. The sentence after the blank describes one of them, the cable-car line. When the second sentence gives one member of a group the first sentence names, 'For example' is the right transition.

A.why: You treated the cable car as a rewording of 'several ways.' The second sentence adds new, narrower information about one approach. It doesn't say the first claim again.

B.why: You chose a concession-and-contrast word, but the cable car doesn't go against the planners' efforts. It is one of them.

D.why: You read the cable car as a conclusion drawn from the first sentence. It is one instance of the planners' efforts, not a result of them.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Marine biologist Kofi Mensah has shown that the cleaner wrasse, a small reef fish that eats parasites off larger fish, changes one habit when another fish is watching. ______ a wrasse being observed by a waiting fish is far less likely to bite off its current client's protective mucus, a form of cheating that wrasses otherwise commit often.
explanation: The first sentence says the wrasse changes 'one habit' but doesn't name it. The sentence after the blank does: when watched, the wrasse stops biting its client's mucus. That describes the same single habit exactly, so 'Specifically' is correct.

A.why: You treated the mucus-biting behavior as one example among many. The passage mentions only 'one habit,' and the second sentence tells you what that habit is.

B.why: You chose a contrast word, but the second sentence doesn't go against Mensah's finding. It states the finding in detail.

C.why: You read the sentences as a sequence of events. Biting less isn't something that happens after the change in habit. It is the change.
